name: shaker_pulse
description: Indian hand cymbals (manjira) pulse on every eighth, louder on the backbeat in the lift and the return.
character: A pair of small Indian hand cymbals struck on every eighth for the pulse, louder on the backbeat in the lift: a soft metallic ring that keeps time and fills the gaps between the plucked notes without pushing energy into the band where the ear is most sensitive.
sources: KB pan-indian (hand cymbals and small percussion keep the tala pulse)
KB african (a steady high pulse under the tune: the hosho in Shona music)

MEASURED: the SoundFont hosho/shaker sample puts 14.9 dB more power in 2.5-5 kHz than in 0.5-2.5 kHz and failed spectral.equal_loudness through three EQ attempts; the guiro decays to digital silence between hits (230 dropouts); the splash-cymbal "zil" sample made 13 click events in the mastered file against 6 for the manjira sample (a leave-one-out through the real mix and master), so the manjira carries the pulse
ESTIMATE: level and placement are starting values

STARTING VALUE: low-pass at 4.5 kHz: a phone speaker returns little above about 5 kHz (KB short-form-functional-music), and the sharp edges of plucked and struck onsets above it are what the click row reacts to

CARRIED OVER from the ringtone project 'Confluence', where each filter, fade and level in this preset was set by a measurement (click count, stem.dropout, equal_loudness); not re-measured for the alarm until the gate runs
